evals.prompt: We gaan releasen naar productie. Het project heeft docs/release-process.md (ff-push acceptance naar main, semver-tag, GitLab Release), de laatste tag is v1.1.2 en acceptance staat 14 commits voor op main zonder migratie. CONVENTIONS.md noemt Slack-kanaal #klant-website (C0123). Vorige week ging er een mail 'Release V1.1.0' naar zes mensen.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the runbook, the scope and the tracker versions, then asks in one AskUserQuestion call for the recipients (proposing the six from the previous release mail), whether to share in #klant-website, and the version. It shows one plan block with the start-mail draft text and waits for the go. After the go it creates a Gmail draft (not sent) and pauses until the user confirms the start mail is out, before any push to main.
assertions: The skill reads docs/release-process.md before planning
Recipients are asked, with the previous release mail's recipients as the proposal
Sharing in the Slack channel from CONVENTIONS.md is proposed as a question, not done unasked
One plan block is shown and nothing is written before the go
The start mail is created as a Gmail draft and never sent
The start mail gives a one-hour indication and says editors can keep working, since no migration is in scope
No promotion to main happens before the user confirms the start mail is out or skips it

evals.prompt: Geef de tickets die mee zijn gegaan in de laatste release een versie en zet ze op done. De nieuwste tag v1.1.2 is een hotfix zonder ticketkeys; v1.1.0 bevat RFW-291, RFW-294 en RFW-305 in commit subjects, RFW-304 staat al op Done, RFW-295 heeft nog een open draft-MR, en RFW-218 komt alleen voor in een MR-beschrijving als context. Het Jira-project heeft geen versies en het aanmaken van een versie geeft 404 "Project with key 'null'".
evals.expected_output: The skill treats this as the after-the-fact path: it lists the recent tags with their ticket counts and takes v1.1.0, the newest tag with ticket work, naming that choice. RFW-291, RFW-294 and RFW-305 get the label v1.1.0 (existing labels kept) and move to Done through a transition whose target is in the done category; RFW-304 gets the label only; RFW-295 is kept open as partial with the open MR as reason; RFW-218 is classified as context and untouched. The recap says a project admin can create the Jira version later.
assertions: v1.1.0 is chosen over the hotfix tag v1.1.2, and the choice is stated
After the 404 on version creation the skill falls back to the label v1.1.0
Existing labels are kept when the label is added
RFW-291, RFW-294 and RFW-305 are transitioned to Done
RFW-304 receives the label but no transition
RFW-295 is not transitioned, and the open MR is given as the reason
RFW-218 is not changed
The result is verified with a JQL query on the label

evals.prompt: Start de release voor dit project.
evals.expected_output: With no docs/release-process.md and no runbook pointer in CONVENTIONS.md, the skill stops before any write and asks how this project releases (which branch deploys production, versioned or not), offering to record the answer in docs/release-process.md.
assertions: The skill looks for docs/release-process.md and a runbook pointer in CONVENTIONS.md
No branch, tag, mail draft or tracker write is created
The skill asks which branch deploys production and whether releases are versioned
The skill offers to record the answer in docs/release-process.md

evals.prompt: Release starten. docs/release-process.md beschrijft een fast-forward van acceptance naar main, maar het project heeft geen tags, geen CHANGELOG.md en CONVENTIONS.md zegt niets over versies. Er gaan 11 commits mee, verzameld over drie weken.
evals.expected_output: Because the project releases in batches and records no versioning decision, the skill asks once whether to introduce versions, recommending a setup MR now with the next release as the first versioned one, next to 'not now' and 'no versions, record that'. This release stays unversioned whatever the answer: the mails name it by date and the tracker only offers Done. When the user picks the introduction, the plan lists the setup MR through skills/create-pr (CHANGELOG.md, a versioning section in the runbook, the CONVENTIONS.md decision line) and a baseline tag on the current production commit.
assertions: The skill asks whether to introduce versions, with the setup MR as the recommended option
The question offers 'not now' and 'no versions, record that' as alternatives
This release is not given a version number and no CHANGELOG or runbook change lands in the release commit
The start mail names the release by date
On 'introduce', the plan contains a setup MR through skills/create-pr and a baseline tag on the production commit
On 'no versions', exactly one decision line is added to CONVENTIONS.md
